items.title: Ralph Sutton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995
items.q: Lee Wiley was married to Jess Stacey at the time.

ctx.x: Who are some of the singers that you’ve played behind that you enjoyed.

Jimmy Rushing. He was one of my favorites. Well Jack Teagarden sang. I remember working at the Village Vanguard behind Maxine Sullivan, who I adored. And there’s another girl singer, Chippy Hill, yeah. But Lee Wiley, I remember I played behind her at the Village Vanguard with Max Kaminsky and Arthur Trappier, he took Slick Jones’ place on drums with Fats Waller. We were working as a trio at the Vanguard and Lee Wiley was married to Jess Stacey at the time. And she came in, she was on the show at the Village…

thinking, I’m going to stay away from singers, man. But anyway, I loved Lee singing you know. I’ll never forget her coming into Eddie Condon’s club later on. I can’t say what our conversation was about, I mean we were very friendly. But she sort of apologized to me for being very sarcastic sometimes on the job you know. But we settled it. There was no problem.
